answer.rationale: Sole cycle decision must cover a 14-day hard expiry with the line at 94% and no buffer, so defer or add-second-source as the only move would lapse primary supply and raise delivery risk. A primary switch is likewise ruled out despite c2’s past unit-cost win: onboarding under no buffer would increase delivery risk and therefore TCO. Incumbent renewal (c1) protects continuity but, given their refusal to reopen price, does not pursue the mandated spend cut. c4 and c6 say the remaining lever is renewal itself—benchmarking plus a longer volume term that previously cut unit cost without shrinking service. Intend to negotiate those terms rather than renew as-is or switch. Verifying c4 because the mid-cycle refusal makes the claim that renewal leverage still moves price the critical uncertainty; 14 days left means a failed negotiation is itself a downstream-supply risk.
